hand: ALOHA parallel gripper (by platform convention, not re-specified); Bi-arm Franka parallel gripper; Apollo humanoid multi-finger dexterous hand (grasp types shown: single-finger push, cylindrical side grasp, medium wrap, five-finger power grasp, bimanual grasp/rotate; no DoF or vendor model given for any embodiment)
arm: ALOHA (bimanual); Bi-arm Franka (bimanual industrial arm); Apollo (full-size bimanual humanoid)
sim: MuJoCo (used to generate evaluation scenes at scale, not for training; engine timestep/contact model not stated)
success_criterion: task-specific progress-score rubric (e.g. 1.00 correct pick+place, 0.50 partial credit variants, 0.00 otherwise), plus a separate binary success rate reported alongside every progress-score figure
headline_metric: progress score / success rate by generalization axis (In-Distribution/Instruction/Action/Visual/Task Generalization), A/B/n real-robot testing
headline_value: ALOHA GR 1.5 progress scores 0.83/0.81/0.73/0.76/0.67 (success rates 0.72/0.71/0.63/0.67/0.62); Bi-arm Franka progress scores 0.74/0.77/0.73/0.70/0.50; Apollo Humanoid progress scores 0.74/0.73/0.66/0.62/0.63 (success rates 0.64/0.64/0.56/0.51/0.40), all vs. GRoD baseline substantially lower on every axis (Figs. 3/35)
note_gaps: No parameter counts for either backbone, no reward/loss function, no observation vector, no domain-randomization list, no action-chunk length or control-rate Hz, and no per-condition trial counts are given anywhere (only '>90% of evaluation episodes were conducted in simulation').
backbone: Gemini ("latest generation of Gemini", Comanici et al. 2025; no separate name beyond "Gemini Robotics 1.5"/"Gemini Robotics-ER 1.5")
action_head: continuous numerical action-value output ("Gemini Robotics 1.5 generates continuous numerical values that represent robot actions, and additionally text when thinking mode is enabled"); no diffusion, flow-matching, or discrete-token terminology used; a "Thinking VLA" interleaves natural-language reasoning traces with action output, paired with a separate embodied-reasoning VLM (GR-ER 1.5) orchestrator via a new "Motion Transfer" training recipe
pretrain_data: multi-embodiment robot data collected on ALOHA, Bi-arm Franka, and Apollo humanoid (thousands of diverse tasks) plus publicly available internet text, image, and video datasets
dexterous_evidence: "Controlling a humanoid is much more challenging than the Aloha or the bi-arm Franka robots, due to higher degree-of-freedom whole-body control, multi-finger dexterity, and limited visibility of the workspace that requires active perception." (§B.2.3.2) — and the Apollo humanoid's progress score and success rate are quantitatively reported by generalization axis (Fig. 3/35) and in the Motion Transfer/Thinking ablations (Fig. 4/6/36/37), unlike the predecessor paper's qualitative-only Apollo result.
